```{r}
## =========================================================
## Harmonize Targeted Metabolomics (All Cohorts) - Clean .R
## =========================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(data.table)
})

## ---------- Helpers ----------
# Use a single reporting threshold across studies:
# prefer LOQ when available, otherwise fall back to LOD.
pick_reporting_limit <- function(lod = NA, loq = NA) {
  lod <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(lod))
  loq <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(loq))
  dplyr::coalesce(loq, lod)
}

collect_lod_summary <- function(data, study_name) {
  child_id <- if ("Child_PID" %in% names(data)) as.character(data$Child_PID) else rep(NA_character_, nrow(data))
  mat_id <- if ("Mat_PID" %in% names(data)) as.character(data$Mat_PID) else rep(NA_character_, nrow(data))
  person_id <- dplyr::coalesce(child_id, mat_id)
  analyte_code <- if ("Analyte_Code" %in% names(data)) as.character(data$Analyte_Code) else rep(NA_character_, nrow(data))
  chemical_group <- if ("Chemical_Group" %in% names(data)) as.character(data$Chemical_Group) else rep(NA_character_, nrow(data))
  units <- if ("Units" %in% names(data)) as.character(data$Units) else rep(NA_character_, nrow(data))
  conc <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(data$Concentration))
  lod <- if ("LOD" %in% names(data)) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(data$LOD)) else rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  
  tibble(
    Study = study_name,
    Person_ID = person_id,
    Chemical_Group = chemical_group,
    Analyte_Code = analyte_code,
    Units = units,
    Concentration = conc,
    LOD = lod
  ) %>%
    filter(!Analyte_Code %in% c("CRE", "SG"), !is.na(Concentration)) %>%
    mutate(
      Has_Limit = !is.na(LOD) & LOD > 0,
      Below_LOD = Has_Limit & Concentration <= LOD
    ) %>%
    group_by(Study, Chemical_Group, Analyte_Code, Units) %>%
    summarise(
      N_People_Total = n_distinct(Person_ID[!is.na(Person_ID)]),
      N_People_With_Limit = n_distinct(Person_ID[Has_Limit & !is.na(Person_ID)]),
      N_People_Below_LOD = n_distinct(Person_ID[Below_LOD & !is.na(Person_ID)]),
      Pct_People_Below_LOD = ifelse(N_People_With_Limit > 0, 100 * N_People_Below_LOD / N_People_With_Limit, NA_real_),
      N_Results_Total = n(),
      N_Results_With_Limit = sum(Has_Limit),
      N_Results_Below_LOD = sum(Below_LOD),
      Pct_Results_Below_LOD = ifelse(N_Results_With_Limit > 0, 100 * N_Results_Below_LOD / N_Results_With_Limit, NA_real_),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

collect_lod_any_summary <- function(data, study_name) {
  child_id <- if ("Child_PID" %in% names(data)) as.character(data$Child_PID) else rep(NA_character_, nrow(data))
  mat_id <- if ("Mat_PID" %in% names(data)) as.character(data$Mat_PID) else rep(NA_character_, nrow(data))
  person_id <- dplyr::coalesce(child_id, mat_id)
  analyte_code <- if ("Analyte_Code" %in% names(data)) as.character(data$Analyte_Code) else rep(NA_character_, nrow(data))
  conc <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(data$Concentration))
  lod <- if ("LOD" %in% names(data)) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(data$LOD)) else rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  is_adjustment_marker <- analyte_code %in% c("CRE", "SG")
  has_result <- !is_adjustment_marker & !is.na(conc)
  has_limit <- has_result & !is.na(lod) & lod > 0
  below_lod <- has_limit & conc <= lod
  people_with_ids <- !is.na(person_id)

  tibble(
    Study = study_name,
    N_People_Total = dplyr::n_distinct(person_id[has_result & people_with_ids]),
    N_People_With_Any_Limit = dplyr::n_distinct(person_id[has_limit & people_with_ids]),
    N_People_Below_Any_LOD = dplyr::n_distinct(person_id[below_lod & people_with_ids]),
    Pct_People_Below_Any_LOD = ifelse(dplyr::n_distinct(person_id[has_limit & people_with_ids]) > 0,
                                      100 * dplyr::n_distinct(person_id[below_lod & people_with_ids]) / dplyr::n_distinct(person_id[has_limit & people_with_ids]),
                                      NA_real_),
    N_Results_Total = sum(has_result),
    N_Results_With_Limit = sum(has_limit),
    N_Results_Below_LOD = sum(below_lod),
    Pct_Results_Below_LOD = ifelse(sum(has_limit) > 0, 100 * sum(below_lod) / sum(has_limit), NA_real_)
  )
}

censor_to_limit <- function(conc, lim) {
  lim <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(lim))
  ifelse(!is.na(lim) & lim > 0 & (is.na(conc) | conc < lim), lim, conc)
}

detected_flag <- function(conc, lim) {
  lim <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(lim))
  ifelse(!is.na(lim) & lim > 0, !is.na(conc) & conc >= lim, NA)
}

## DILUTION ADJUSTMENT SWITCH (2026-11-03).
## cre_correct() divides by creatinine in mg/dL with no x100, so CRE-corrected
## cohorts land ~50-200x below SG-corrected and unadjusted cohorts while still
## labelled ng/mL. That is fine within a cohort but distorts every between-cohort
## comparison. Set HHEAR_DILUTION_ADJUST=FALSE to build an UNADJUSTED copy for
## between-cohort analyses, and HHEAR_HARMONIZED_OUT to write it somewhere other
## than Input/Harmonized_Datasets.
## HHEAR_DILUTION_ADJUST=UGG is a sensitivity variant: creatinine-corrected values
## are multiplied by 100, i.e. (ng/mL)/(mg/dL) -> ug/g creatinine, which puts
## them on the same order of magnitude as SG-normalized and raw ng/mL. Every
## cohort's creatinine is mg/dL (checked 2026-11-03), so x100 is uniform.
## DEFAULT CHANGED 2026-11-03 to UGG (author's decision): ug/g creatinine is the
## canonical build. TRUE reproduces the pre-2026-11-03 mg/dL-divided data
## (backed up in Input/Harmonized_Datasets/_backup_2026-11-03_pre_ugg/).
## Rebuild via Coding/rebuild_harmonized_targeted.sh, which also adds the
## Dilution_Adjustment column.
DILUTION_MODE   <- toupper(Sys.getenv("HHEAR_DILUTION_ADJUST", "UGG"))
stopifnot(DILUTION_MODE %in% c("TRUE", "FALSE", "UGG"))
DILUTION_ADJUST <- DILUTION_MODE != "FALSE"
CRE_SCALE       <- if (DILUTION_MODE == "UGG") 100 else 1
HARMONIZED_OUT  <- Sys.getenv("HHEAR_HARMONIZED_OUT", "../Input/Harmonized_Datasets")
message("Dilution adjustment: ", DILUTION_MODE, "  -> writing to ", HARMONIZED_OUT)

sg_correct <- function(conc, sg, target = 1.020) {
  if (!DILUTION_ADJUST) return(conc)
  ifelse(is.na(sg) | sg <= 1, conc, conc * ((target - 1)/(sg - 1)))
}

cre_correct <- function(conc, cre) {
  if (!DILUTION_ADJUST) return(conc)
  ifelse(!is.na(cre) & cre > 0, CRE_SCALE * conc/cre, conc)
}

to_ng_per_mL <- function(value, units) {
  case_when(
    is.na(units)            ~ value,
    units %in% c("ng/mL")   ~ value,
    units %in% c("ug/dL")   ~ value * 10,
    units %in% c("ng/L")    ~ value / 1000,
    units %in% c("pg/mL","pg/ml") ~ value / 1000,
    units %in% c("mg/L")    ~ value * 1000,
    TRUE ~ value
  )
}

## NHBCS (combine targeted + Epi PFAS) --------------------
# MATRIX SEPARATION (2026-08, revised): NHBCS carries PFAS from TWO DIFFERENT
# BIOLOGICAL MATRICES, not two assays of the same thing:
#   * NHBCS_Targeted  -> Sample_matrix == "BR" (breast milk), all 9 SPFAS analytes
#   * NHBCS_Epi       -> serum/plasma (pivoted below)
# Breast-milk PFOS 0.024 vs serum 2.60 is a ~1% milk:serum ratio, which is the
# documented partitioning -- the low values are physiology, NOT a failed assay.
#
# The bug was that bind_rows() put both under the same Analyte_Code, so the
# pipeline's group_by(Study, PID, Analyte_Code) %>% mean() AVERAGED milk with
# serum (PFOS entered analyses at 0.957 instead of 2.60).
#
# Fix: tag the breast-milk codes with a _BR suffix so they can never pool with
# serum, but are retained rather than discarded. Same approach as ATLAA's _DBS.
# Applied to ALL 9, not just the 4 that overlap Epi -- PFBS/PFHP/PFHX/PFUN are
# measured in SERUM by other cohorts, so they were silently pooling too.
#
# NOTE: PFHX has 2 rows per person (852/426) differing only in LOQ (0.01 vs
# 0.025) and Comment_code (0 vs 211). Both are non-detects; left as-is because
# Comment_code 211 is undocumented here. Worth checking against NHBCS's codebook.
NHBCS_Targeted_Targ <- NHBCS_data_list[["NHBCS_Targeted"]] %>%
  mutate(Analyte_Code = if_else(Chemical_Group == "SPFAS",
                                paste0(Analyte_Code, "_BR"), Analyte_Code)) %>%
  transmute(Mat_PID = Mother_pid, Chemical_Group, Analyte_Code, Concentration, Units, LOD = LOQ,Sample_Collection_Year = sample_collection_year) %>%
  mutate(Detected = detected_flag(Concentration, LOD),
         Concentration = censor_to_limit(Concentration, LOD))

NHBCS_Targeted_Epi <- NHBCS_data_list[["NHBCS_Epi"]] %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = 16:22, names_to = "Analyte_Code", values_to = "Concentration") %>%
  transmute(Mat_PID = mother_pid, Analyte_Code, Concentration)

NHBCS_Targeted_PreAdjust <- bind_rows(NHBCS_Targeted_Targ, NHBCS_Targeted_Epi)
lod_summary_list[["NHBCS_Targeted"]] <- collect_lod_summary(NHBCS_Targeted_PreAdjust, "NHBCS_Targeted")
NHBCS_Targeted <- NHBCS_Targeted_PreAdjust

    Mat_PID = PID, Chemical_Group, Analyte_Code, Concentration, Units, LOD,
    sample_collection_timepoint,Sample_Collection_Year = sample_collection_year
  )
lod_summary_list[["nuMoM2b_Targeted"]] <- collect_lod_summary(nuMoM2b_Targeted_raw, "nuMoM2b_Targeted")

nuMoM2b_Targeted <- nuMoM2b_Targeted_raw %>%

nuMoM2b_Targeted <- nuMoM2b_Targeted %>%

## TEDDY (CRE correction) ---------------------------------
TEDDY_Targeted_raw <- TEDDY_data_list[["TEDDY_Targeted"]] %>%
  # UNITS CORRECTION (2026-08): TEDDY's UPAH panel (NAP1, NAP2, PYR1) is
  # labelled "ng/mL" but the values are numerically ng/L. Evidence:
  #  * raw medians 588 / 1670 / 80 sit in the same numeric range as the cohorts
  #    that DO report ng/L (GRAPHS 1890/6075/894, DCHS 870/5980/290,
  #    SICAS 609/4690/126) rather than 1000x above them;
  #  * TEDDY's reported LODs (150 / 800 / 100) likewise match SICAS's ng/L LODs
  #    (200 / 100 / 20) -- a genuine ng/mL panel would imply a detection limit
  #    ~1000x worse than the same assay elsewhere;
  #  * across the 36 analytes TEDDY shares with other creatinine-corrected
  #    cohorts the median ratio is 2x, but PYR1/NAP1/NAP2 are 1123x/901x/463x;
  #  * every other TEDDY chemical group has a median of 0.19-9.59 (normal for
  #    ng/mL); only UPAH sits at 511.
  # Scope is deliberately narrow: UPAH only, TEDDY only. Re-check against the
  # TEDDY data dictionary if one becomes available.
  mutate(Units = if_else(Chemical_Group == "UPAH" & Units == "ng/mL", "ng/L", Units)) %>%
  transmute(
    Child_PID = PID, Chemical_Group, Analyte_Code, Concentration, Units, LOD,
    Sample_collection_timepoint,Sample_Collection_Year = Sample_collection_year
  )
lod_summary_list[["TEDDY_Targeted"]] <- collect_lod_summary(TEDDY_Targeted_raw, "TEDDY_Targeted")

TEDDY_Targeted <- TEDDY_Targeted_raw %>%
  filter(Analyte_Code != "CRE") %>%
  mutate(Detected = detected_flag(Concentration, LOD),
         Concentration = censor_to_limit(Concentration, LOD))

TEDDY_CRE <- TEDDY_Targeted_raw %>%
  filter(Analyte_Code == "CRE") %>% 
  transmute(Child_PID, Sample_collection_timepoint, Concentration_CRE = Concentration)

TEDDY_Targeted <- TEDDY_Targeted %>%
  left_join(TEDDY_CRE, by = c("Child_PID","Sample_collection_timepoint")) %>%
  mutate(Concentration = cre_correct(Concentration, Concentration_CRE),
         LOD = cre_correct(LOD, Concentration_CRE)) %>%
  select(-Concentration_CRE, -Sample_collection_timepoint)
```

```{r}
## =========================================================
## NEW COHORTS (added 2026-08): GRAPHS, ATLAA, SWSD
## Each produces a canonical <COHORT>_Targeted object which the auto-bind
## below (ls pattern "^..._Targeted$") picks up with no further edits.
## IMHRD is intentionally excluded: it is aggregated year-level summary data
## (no participant IDs / per-sample concentrations) and cannot enter a
## participant-level harmonization. See HHEAR_Dataset_Creation.Rmd.
## =========================================================

## GRAPHS (maternal urine; CRE correction, joined per-sample on SID) --------
GRAPHS_Targeted_raw <- GRAPHS_data_list[["GRAPHS_Targeted"]] %>%
  transmute(
    Mat_PID = PID,
    SID,
    Chemical_Group,
    Analyte_Code,
    Concentration,
    Units,                                        # NOTE: VOCs are pmol/mL (not handled by to_ng_per_mL)
    LOD = pick_reporting_limit(LOD, LOQ),
    Sample_Collection_Year = sample_collection_year
  )
lod_summary_list[["GRAPHS_Targeted"]] <- collect_lod_summary(GRAPHS_Targeted_raw, "GRAPHS_Targeted")

GRAPHS_Targeted <- GRAPHS_Targeted_raw %>%
  filter(Analyte_Code != "CRE") %>%
  mutate(Detected = detected_flag(Concentration, LOD),
         Concentration = censor_to_limit(Concentration, LOD))

GRAPHS_CRE <- GRAPHS_Targeted_raw %>%
  filter(Analyte_Code == "CRE") %>%
  transmute(Mat_PID, SID, Concentration_CRE = Concentration)

GRAPHS_Targeted <- GRAPHS_Targeted %>%
  left_join(GRAPHS_CRE, by = c("Mat_PID","SID")) %>%
  mutate(Concentration = cre_correct(Concentration, Concentration_CRE),
         LOD = cre_correct(LOD, Concentration_CRE)) %>%
  select(-Concentration_CRE)
  # KEEP SID: GRAPHS has 898 distinct (PID, SID) samples across 300 mothers and
  # most PID x year combinations contain MORE THAN ONE sample, so dropping SID
  # would leave thousands of rows that are exact duplicates on
  # (Mat_PID, Analyte_Code, Sample_Collection_Year) and destroy repeat-sample
  # identity. Retained the same way SWSD retains `trimester`. Downstream the
  # quantile pipeline still collapses to one value per participant per analyte
  # via group_by(Study, PID, Analyte_Code) %>% mean().

## ATLAA (maternal PFAS; serum T1/T2 + DBS; pre-imputed, no LOD) -------------
## Sample_Matrix / Timepoint are carried through (NA for other cohorts via
## rbindlist fill=TRUE). CHECK: downstream per-participant summaries that
## group_by(Study, PID, Analyte_Code) will pool serum T1/T2 and DBS unless
## matrix/timepoint handling is added.
ATLAA_Targeted_raw <- ATLAA_data_list[["ATLAA_Targeted"]] %>%
  transmute(
    Mat_PID = PID,
    Chemical_Group,
    Analyte_Code,
    Concentration,
    Units,
    LOD,                                          # reconstructed LOD (=imputed floor*sqrt(2))
    Sample_Matrix,
    Timepoint,
    Sample_Collection_Year = NA_real_             # no collection year provided
  )
lod_summary_list[["ATLAA_Targeted"]] <- collect_lod_summary(ATLAA_Targeted_raw, "ATLAA_Targeted")

ATLAA_Targeted <- ATLAA_Targeted_raw %>%
  mutate(Detected = detected_flag(Concentration, LOD))
  # No censor_to_limit(): concentrations are already provider-imputed to
  # LOD/sqrt(2). The censored-quantile engine downstream uses Detected + LOD.

## SWSD (maternal urine neonicotinoids; CRE correction per subject x trimester)
## Trimester is carried through so repeated measures stay distinguishable.
SWSD_Targeted_raw <- SWSD_data_list[["SWSD_Targeted"]] %>%
  transmute(
    Mat_PID = PID,
    trimester,
    Chemical_Group,
    Analyte_Code,
    Concentration,
    Units,
    LOD,                                          # reconstructed LOD (=imputed floor*sqrt(2))
    Sample_Collection_Year = NA_real_             # no collection year provided
  )
lod_summary_list[["SWSD_Targeted"]] <- collect_lod_summary(SWSD_Targeted_raw, "SWSD_Targeted")

SWSD_Targeted <- SWSD_Targeted_raw %>%
  filter(Analyte_Code != "CRE") %>%
  mutate(Detected = detected_flag(Concentration, LOD))
  # No censor_to_limit(): concentrations already provider-imputed to LOD/sqrt(2).

SWSD_CRE <- SWSD_Targeted_raw %>%
  filter(Analyte_Code == "CRE") %>%
  transmute(Mat_PID, trimester, Concentration_CRE = Concentration)

SWSD_Targeted <- SWSD_Targeted %>%
  left_join(SWSD_CRE, by = c("Mat_PID","trimester")) %>%
  mutate(Concentration = cre_correct(Concentration, Concentration_CRE),
         LOD = cre_correct(LOD, Concentration_CRE)) %>%
  select(-Concentration_CRE)          # keep 'trimester' to distinguish repeated measures

```


```{r}
## =========================================================
## Final bind & save
## =========================================================
if (exists("Targeted_Data_All")) rm(Targeted_Data_All)

tgt_names <- ls(envir = .GlobalEnv, pattern = "^[A-Za-z0-9._]+_Targeted$")
# drop helper or raw suffixes if any slipped in
tgt_names <- tgt_names[!grepl("_Targeted_(SG|CRE|raw|Raw)$", tgt_names)]

bind_list <- mget(tgt_names, envir = .GlobalEnv)

Targeted_Data_All <- rbindlist(bind_list, use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE, idcol = "Study") %>%
  # Participant IDs are CHARACTER across all harmonized artifacts (2026-08).
  # Some cohorts (e.g. ATLAA) use alphanumeric IDs such as "E0604", so rbindlist
  # would coerce the column to character anyway; doing it EXPLICITLY here makes the
  # type deterministic regardless of which cohorts are present, instead of silently
  # flipping numeric->character the first time an alphanumeric-ID cohort is added.
  # Harmonized_SDOH and Harmonized_Outcomes apply the same coercion.
  mutate(across(any_of(c("Child_PID","Mat_PID")), as.character)) %>%
  # One cohort (MDUC / HAPTOGLOBIN, 406 rows) ships "ug/mL" with the micro sign
  # stored as a RAW LATIN1 BYTE (0xB5). That is invalid UTF-8: it makes grepl()
  # error with "unable to translate ... to a wide string" and it crashes gridtext
  # ("has encountered a tag that isn't supported yet: <c3>"), which blocks
  # Intervals_ByCountry.Rmd and leaves Figure 1's country-interval panel stale.
  # Normalise ONLY the strings that are invalid UTF-8, to ASCII "ug/mL".
  # Values are unchanged: to_ng_per_mL() did not convert this unit before and
  # does not now -- this is purely an encoding/label repair. (2026-08)
  # NOTE: no literal non-ASCII character appears below on purpose -- writing the
  # micro sign into this source file makes the pattern itself invalid once purled.
  # iconv(..., to = "ASCII", sub = "u") maps the latin1 micro byte to "u",
  # turning the bad string into plain "ug/mL".
  mutate(Units = {
    .u <- Units
    .bad <- !is.na(.u) & is.na(iconv(.u, "UTF-8", "UTF-8"))
    if (any(.bad)) .u[.bad] <- iconv(.u[.bad], from = "latin1", to = "ASCII", sub = "u")
    .u
  }) %>%
  # Implausible collection years -> NA (2026-08).
  # DISCOVER ships 9 rows dated 1905 -- 9 analytes for a SINGLE participant,
  # while every other DISCOVER row is 2009-2019. It is a data-entry/parsing
  # artefact, but it silently set the lower bound of the study-wide collection
  # year range reported in the manuscript ("1985 to 2020" became 1905-2021).
  # HHEAR biospecimen collection starts in the 1980s (NYUWHS, 1985), so
  # anything before 1980 cannot be a real collection year. NA rather than a
  # guess: the row's CONCENTRATION is still usable, only its date is not.
  mutate(Sample_Collection_Year = if_else(
    !is.na(Sample_Collection_Year) & Sample_Collection_Year < 1980,
    NA_real_, as.numeric(Sample_Collection_Year))) %>%
  relocate(any_of(c("Study","Child_PID","Mat_PID","Chemical_Group","Analyte_Code",
                    "Detected","Concentration","Units","LOD")))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Sample matrix (2026-08-10)
##
## The raw HHEAR TARGETED_DATA files all carry a `Sample_matrix` column, and the
## readers preserve it -- 37 of 40 targeted objects in Input/*_Data_All.RData
## have it. It was being lost HERE: the 68 per-cohort transmute() calls above
## each name their columns explicitly and none of them names it.
##
## Losing it forced every downstream consumer to infer matrix from the
## Chemical_Group prefix, which is only a proxy. That proxy is wrong often
## enough to matter: it classifies CCREOH as blood via "BTE" but cannot tell
## you CCREOH is WHOLE BLOOD, and it silently pools house dust (PROGRESS) with
## biospecimens.
##
## Rather than edit 68 transmutes, the field is re-attached by a join. This is
## safe because matrix is fully determined by (Study, Analyte_Code): checked
## across all 891 (object, analyte) pairs in the source lists, ZERO have more
## than one matrix. A study measuring phthalates in urine and PFAS in serum is
## handled correctly, because the key includes the analyte.
##
## Values arrive in two conventions -- HHEAR specimen codes (U, S, P, WB, RBC,
## BR, DBS) and spelled-out names (URINE, SERUM, PLASMA, WHOLE BLOOD) -- so
## they are normalised to the README glossary vocabulary. Matrix_Class is the
## coarse grouping most analyses actually want.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Read the lookup back from Input/*_Data_All.RData rather than from memory:
## several cohort blocks rm() their *_data_list once used, so the objects are
## not reliably in scope here.
.matrix_lookup <- local({
  # same discovery the loader at the top of this file uses
  files <- list.files("../Input/", pattern = "All\\.RData$",
                      recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  out <- list()
  for (f in files) {
    e <- new.env()
    ok <- tryCatch({ load(f, envir = e); TRUE }, error = function(err) FALSE)
    if (!ok) next
    for (obj in ls(e)) {
      L <- get(obj, envir = e)
      if (!is.list(L)) next
      for (nm in names(L)) {
        d <- L[[nm]]
        if (!is.data.frame(d) || !grepl("Targeted", nm)) next
        mc <- grep("^sample_matrix$", names(d), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
        ac <- grep("^analyte_code$",  names(d), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
        if (!length(mc) || !length(ac)) next
        out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(
          Study        = nm,
          Analyte_Code = as.character(d[[ac[1]]]),
          .raw_matrix  = toupper(trimws(as.character(d[[mc[1]]]))),
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      }
    }
  }
  if (!length(out)) return(NULL)
  res <- dplyr::distinct(dplyr::bind_rows(out))
  # A few cohorts are assembled under a different label than their source
  # object: SLC is bound from SLC_2517 + SLC_3131 (urine + plasma), and VIVA's
  # source object is VIVAC. Without these aliases the join silently misses them.
  res$Study <- sub("^SLC_[0-9]+_Targeted$", "SLC_Targeted", res$Study)
  res$Study <- sub("^VIVAC_Targeted$",      "VIVA_Targeted", res$Study)
  # NHBCS's breast-milk PFAS are renamed to *_BR by the cohort block above, but
  # this lookup is read from the raw delivery where they are still unsuffixed.
  # Without the same rename the join lands on the WRONG rows: the unsuffixed
  # codes in the harmonized table are NHBCS_Epi serum, so the four overlapping
  # analytes (PFDA/PFNA/PFOA/PFOS) were being labelled "Breast Milk" while the
  # nine actual breast-milk analytes got no matrix at all.
  res$Analyte_Code <- ifelse(res$Study == "NHBCS_Targeted" & res$.raw_matrix == "BR",
                             paste0(res$Analyte_Code, "_BR"), res$Analyte_Code)
  dplyr::distinct(res)
})

if (!is.null(.matrix_lookup)) {
  .matrix_lookup <- .matrix_lookup %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.raw_matrix), .raw_matrix != "", .raw_matrix != "NA") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Sample_Matrix = dplyr::case_when(
      .raw_matrix %in% c("U", "URINE")               ~ "Urine",
      .raw_matrix %in% c("S", "SERUM", "MATERNAL SERUM") ~ "Serum",
      .raw_matrix %in% c("P", "PLASMA")              ~ "Plasma",
      .raw_matrix %in% c("WB", "WHOLE BLOOD")        ~ "Whole Blood",
      .raw_matrix == "RBC"                           ~ "Red Blood Cells",
      .raw_matrix == "DBS"                           ~ "Dried Blood Spots",
      .raw_matrix == "CB"                            ~ "Cord Blood",
      .raw_matrix == "BC"                            ~ "Buffy Coat",
      .raw_matrix == "BR"                            ~ "Breast Milk",
      .raw_matrix == "DUST"                          ~ "Dust",
      TRUE                                           ~ .raw_matrix)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Matrix_Class = dplyr::case_when(
      Sample_Matrix == "Urine" ~ "Urine",
      Sample_Matrix %in% c("Serum","Plasma","Whole Blood","Red Blood Cells",
                           "Dried Blood Spots","Cord Blood","Buffy Coat") ~ "Blood",
      Sample_Matrix == "Dust" ~ "Non-biological",
      TRUE ~ "Other")) %>%
    dplyr::select(Study, Analyte_Code, Sample_Matrix, Matrix_Class) %>%
    dplyr::distinct()

  ## -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## Five cohorts cannot be covered by the (Study, Analyte_Code) join:
  ##   ELEMENT - source table is WIDE (analytes are columns 7:14), so there is
  ##             no Analyte_Code to key on. Its Sample_matrix is "Urine" for all
  ##             887 source rows, so a study-level value is exact, not a guess.
  ##   MEBCO   - raw TARGETED_DATA ships no matrix column.
  ##             README: "Trace Elements in urine".
  ##   TSIC    - raw ships no matrix column.
  ##             README: cotinine and inflammatory markers in children's SALIVA.
  ##   SWSD    - the provider workbook has no matrix column at all; its data
  ##             dictionary states maternal urine.
  ##   OBSS    - raw ships no matrix column, and its README is explicit PER
  ##             ASSAY: serum brominated flame retardants / organochlorines /
  ##             PCBs, and PLASMA perfluoroalkyls. Keyed on Chemical_Group.
  ## Everything here is read off a README or data dictionary, not inferred from
  ## the numbers.
  ## -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  .matrix_study <- data.frame(
    Study = c("ELEMENT_Targeted", "MEBCO_Targeted", "TSIC_Targeted", "SWSD_Targeted"),
    .study_matrix = c("Urine", "Urine", "Saliva", "Urine"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  .matrix_obss <- data.frame(
    Study = "OBSS_Targeted",
    Chemical_Group = c("PBFR", "SOC", "SPCB", "SPFAS"),
    .grp_matrix = c("Serum", "Serum", "Serum", "Plasma"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  # ATLAA already sets Sample_Matrix in its reader; drop the old column first so
  # the join is the single source of truth and cannot produce .x/.y duplicates.
  Targeted_Data_All <- Targeted_Data_All %>%
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("Sample_Matrix", "Matrix_Class"))) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(.matrix_lookup %>% dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("Matrix_Class")),
                     by = c("Study", "Analyte_Code")) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(.matrix_study, by = "Study") %>%
    dplyr::left_join(.matrix_obss,  by = c("Study", "Chemical_Group")) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Sample_Matrix = dplyr::coalesce(Sample_Matrix, .grp_matrix, .study_matrix)) %>%
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c(".study_matrix", ".grp_matrix"))) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Matrix_Class = dplyr::case_when(
      Sample_Matrix == "Urine" ~ "Urine",
      Sample_Matrix %in% c("Serum","Plasma","Whole Blood","Red Blood Cells",
                           "Dried Blood Spots","Cord Blood","Buffy Coat") ~ "Blood",
      Sample_Matrix == "Dust" ~ "Non-biological",
      is.na(Sample_Matrix) ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ "Other"))

  message(sprintf("Sample_Matrix attached: %.1f%% of rows, %d of %d studies",
                  100 * mean(!is.na(Targeted_Data_All$Sample_Matrix)),
                  dplyr::n_distinct(Targeted_Data_All$Study[!is.na(Targeted_Data_All$Sample_Matrix)]),
                  dplyr::n_distinct(Targeted_Data_All$Study)))
}

Targeted_LOD_Summary <- bind_rows(lod_summary_list) %>%
  mutate(
    Pct_People_Below_LOD = round(Pct_People_Below_LOD, 1),
    Pct_Results_Below_LOD = round(Pct_Results_Below_LOD, 1)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Pct_People_Below_LOD), desc(Pct_Results_Below_LOD), Study, Analyte_Code)

lod_fold_change_flag <- 10

Targeted_Study_Analyte_LOD <- Targeted_Data_All %>%
  filter(!Analyte_Code %in% c("CRE", "SG")) %>%
  mutate(LOD = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(LOD))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(LOD), LOD > 0) %>%
  group_by(Study, Chemical_Group, Analyte_Code, Units) %>%
  summarise(
    N_Results_With_LOD = n(),
    N_Unique_LOD_Within_Study = n_distinct(LOD),
    Study_LOD_Min = min(LOD),
    Study_LOD_Median = median(LOD),
    Study_LOD_Max = max(LOD),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Analyte_Code, Study)

Targeted_LOD_CrossStudy_Summary <- Targeted_Study_Analyte_LOD %>%
  group_by(Chemical_Group, Analyte_Code, Units) %>%
  summarise(
    N_Studies = n_distinct(Study),
    Min_Study_LOD = min(Study_LOD_Median),
    Median_Study_LOD = median(Study_LOD_Median),
    Max_Study_LOD = max(Study_LOD_Median),
    LOD_Fold_Difference = max(Study_LOD_Median) / min(Study_LOD_Median),
    Any_Within_Study_LOD_Variation = any(N_Unique_LOD_Within_Study > 1),
    Flag_Wide_CrossStudy_LOD_Difference = LOD_Fold_Difference >= lod_fold_change_flag,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(LOD_Fold_Difference), Analyte_Code, Units)

Targeted_LOD_CrossStudy_Flagged <- Targeted_LOD_CrossStudy_Summary %>%
  filter(Flag_Wide_CrossStudy_LOD_Difference)

dir.create(HARMONIZED_OUT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
save(
  Targeted_Data_All,
  #Targeted_LOD_Summary,
  #Targeted_Study_Analyte_LOD,
  #Targeted_LOD_CrossStudy_Summary,
  #Targeted_LOD_CrossStudy_Flagged,
  file = file.path(HARMONIZED_OUT, "Harmonized_Targeted.RData")
)
## NOTE (2026-08): do NOT write Harmonized_Targeted.csv from here.
## An earlier version of this chunk wrote Targeted_Data_All to
## ../Input/Harmonized_Datasets/Harmonized_Targeted.csv, but that is the WRONG
## target and is destructive:
##   * The CSV-based consumers (Targeted_ExWAS_Replication.Rmd,
##     cohort_regime_diagnostic.R) resolve their input_dir to
##     Health_Outcome_Analysis/Input/, NOT Input/Harmonized_Datasets/.
##   * The existing Input/Harmonized_Datasets/Harmonized_Targeted.csv has a
##     different schema (carries `Limit` and `LOQ`), which the overwrite dropped.
## To propagate new cohorts to the CSV consumers, regenerate
## Health_Outcome_Analysis/Input/Harmonized_Targeted.csv deliberately via
## whatever process produces that file.
write.csv(Targeted_LOD_Summary,
          file = file.path(HARMONIZED_OUT, "Harmonized_Targeted_LOD_Summary.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(Targeted_Study_Analyte_LOD,
          file = file.path(HARMONIZED_OUT, "Harmonized_Targeted_Study_Analyte_LOD.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(Targeted_LOD_CrossStudy_Summary,
          file = file.path(HARMONIZED_OUT, "Harmonized_Targeted_LOD_CrossStudy_Summary.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(Targeted_LOD_CrossStudy_Flagged,
          file = file.path(HARMONIZED_OUT, "Harmonized_Targeted_LOD_CrossStudy_Flagged.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# quick sanity
print(dim(Targeted_Data_All))
print(Targeted_LOD_Summary)
print(Targeted_LOD_CrossStudy_Flagged)
```
